content: To reduce hospital readmissions for individuals with diabetes, the following strategies have been identified: 1. Scheduled Home Health Visits: Regularly scheduled visits by healthcare professionals to the patient’s home can enhance diabetes management and lower the risk of readmissions. These visits allow for close monitoring of the patient’s condition, timely interventions, and reinforcement of self-care practices. 2. Ambulatory Follow-Up Care: Early follow-up appointments after hospital discharge ensure continuity of care. These visits help address potential complications or issues before they escalate into conditions requiring readmission. 3. Targeted Outreach Programs: Programs specifically designed for high-risk individuals, such as those with a history of diabetic ketoacidosis or patients with an A1C level greater than 9% (>75 mmol/mol), can provide tailored support and interventions to prevent readmissions. 4. Transitional Care Model: Adopting a transitional care approach that incorporates collaborative, patient-centered medical homes can significantly reduce readmission rates. This model emphasizes coordinated care during the transition from hospital to home, ensuring that patients receive comprehensive and personalized support.
